definitions.definition: Ttor = reals/(2*pi*integers), with normalized measure dx/(2*pi); spatial products and integrals are on this domain.
For an integrable periodic f, Fourier(f)(k)=hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx; the transform extends to distributions by duality.

For every real s, H^s(Ttor) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials with ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2, <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2). Negative spaces are interpreted as distributions. Homogeneous norms on zero-mean distributions are ||f||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2. Real means hat f(-k)=conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0)=0.

L2=H^0(Ttor), with ||f||_2^2=(2*pi)^(-1) integral |f|^2 dx. More generally L^p uses the same normalized measure; L^infinity is essential supremum. Sequence ell^2 uses counting measure on Z (or Z\{0} when specified). Time suprema use continuous representatives; derivative norms are essential suprema.

definitions.type: Airy group indexed by real time
definitions.definition: S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), hat(S_t f)(k)=exp(i*t*k^3) hat f(k).
P0(f)=hat f(0), identified with a constant function.
Pnz=I-P0, denoted P in the supplied proof. Fourier projections P_leq(N) and P_gt(N) retain |k|<=N and |k|>N respectively, for N>=0.
Dinv=partial_x^(-1) has Fourier multiplier (i*k)^(-1) at nonzero integer k and zero at k=0. Dinv2=(Dinv)^2 is denoted D^(-2).

definitions.type: quadratic update family for positive timestep
definitions.definition: For tau>0 and mean-zero f in L2, Ftau(f)=(1/6)*Pnz[(S_tau Dinv f)^2]-(1/6)*S_tau Pnz[(Dinv f)^2].

definitions.type: cubic update family for positive timestep
definitions.definition: For tau>0 and mean-zero f in L2, Htau(f)=(1/3)*Pnz[(S_tau Dinv f)*Dinv Ftau(f)]+(tau/9)*(S_tau Dinv f)*P0(f^2)-(1/54)*[S_(tau-s) Dinv[(S_s Dinv f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)-(1/(27*tau))*[S_(tau-s) Dinv2[(S_(s-tau) Dinv2 Ftau(f))*(S_s Dinv f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau). Brackets mean the value at tau minus the value at zero. All products are spatial products.

Psi_tau(f)=S_tau f+Ftau(f)+Htau(f). Given mean-zero u0 in L2 and an integer L>=1, set tau=T/L, t_n=n*tau, u^0=u0 and u^(n+1)=Psi_tau(u^n) for 0<=n<L; write v^n=S_(-t_n)u^n. There is no spatial cutoff.

KdV is u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)*partial_x(u^2), u(0)=u0. An exact solution on [0,T] with H^gamma data means the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma(Ttor)) distributional solution obtained by smooth approximation. This describes the convention and asserts no existence. For such a solution write v(t)=S_(-t)u(t), and M=1+sup_[0,T]||v(t)||_(H^gamma).
For tau>0 and real alpha,beta, M_tau g=tau^(-1) integral_0^tau g(s) ds and eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).

definitions.type: averaged cubic trilinear Fourier family, initially on polynomials
definitions.definition: For tau>0, t0 real, and mean-zero polynomial inputs f1,f2,f3, define Remainder_(t0,tau)(f1,f2,f3) to have zero mean and, for k!=0, Fourier coefficient -tau/(18*i*k) sum_(a+b+c=k,a+b!=0) exp(-i*t0*Phi)*eta_tau(alpha,beta)*hat f1(a)*hat f2(b)*hat f3(c), where p=a+b, alpha=3*a*b*p, beta=3*k*c*p and Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3. Its bounded extensions will be proved; R^n_(2,tau) means t0=t_n.
Bop_t(f,g)=S_(-t)*partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)], initially for smooth periodic functions and by distributional product for L2 inputs.
Jop_t(f,g)=S_(-t) Pnz[(S_t Dinv f)(S_t Dinv g)].

For a time interval I=[a,b], Cop_I(f,g,h)=integral_a^b S_(-t) Pnz{Pnz[(S_t f(t))(S_t g(t))]*(S_t Dinv h(t))} dt. Initially this is defined for smooth inputs; the continuous extensions in the source estimates are meant when used for rough inputs.
pstar=23/14.

For an interval I of length at most one, ||f||_X(I)=||f||_(L^infinity(I;L2))+||partial_t f||_(L^infinity(I;H^(-pstar))). Derivatives are distributional time derivatives, with their essential-supremum norms.

For a grid start t_n=n*tau, tau>0, and time-independent mean-zero w, Stage_n(t;w)=(1/2) integral_(t_n)^t Bop_s(w,w) ds for t in [t_n,t_n+tau]. The associated bilinear stage has w1,w2 in its two slots.
For 0<gamma<=1, agamma=1/2-gamma if gamma<1/2, agamma=1/8 if gamma=1/2, and agamma=0 if gamma>1/2.

For smooth mean-zero initial data and tau=T/L>0, on I_n=[t_n,t_(n+1)] put f_n=v^n, F_n(t)=Stage_n(t;f_n), z_n(t)=f_n+F_n(t), C_n(t)=integral_(t_n)^t Bop_s(f_n,F_n(s)) ds, Q_n(t)=(1/2)integral_(t_n)^t Bop_s(F_n(s),F_n(s)) ds, W_n=Q_n(t_(n+1))+Remainder_(t_n,tau)(f_n,f_n,f_n), V(t)=f_n+F_n(t)+C_n(t)+Q_n(t)-(t-t_n)*W_n/tau, and Y_n(t)=V(t)-z_n(t). Put rho_n(t)=-integral_(t_n)^t Bop_s(Y_n,z_n) ds-(1/2)integral_(t_n)^t Bop_s(Y_n,Y_n) ds-(t-t_n)*W_n/tau. Define Rres(0)=0 and concatenate rho_n: Rres(t)=sum_(j<n)rho_j(t_(j+1))+rho_n(t) on I_n. For an exact twisted solution v, set e=v-V, delta_n=||f_n-v(t_n)||_2, q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n. V is initially stepwise defined; continuity is a proved assertion. The per-step formulas define a tuple of functions for any prescribed smooth mean-zero step state f_n, step start n*tau and positive tau, independently of whether f_n comes from a full trajectory. In that local use, any comparison state w may replace v(t_n) in delta_n=||f_n-w||_2 and q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n. Full concatenation, V on the whole time interval and e=v-V concern a full numerical trajectory and an exact solution as specified above.

inputs.statement: S_t is an isometry on every H^s and preserves real functions and zero mean; Fourier projections contract these norms. For mean-zero L2 inputs, ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2, ||Bop_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))<=C||f||_2||g||_2, ||Jop_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2 and ||Jop_t(A,B)||_2<=C||Dinv A||_2||B||_2, uniformly in t. For arbitrary L2 F,G, ||Dinv Pnz(FG)||_2<=C||F||_2||G||_2. For mean-zero A, ||A||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A||_2. H^1 embeds continuously into L^infinity and satisfies ||AB||_(H^1)<=C||A||_(H^1)||B||_(H^1). For time-smooth spatially smooth mean-zero f,g on [a,b], integral_a^b Bop_t(f,g)dt=(1/3)[Jop_t(f,g)]_a^b-(1/3)integral_a^b[Jop_t(f',g)+Jop_t(f,g')]dt. Also Jop is symmetric and integral_I Jop_t(Bop_t(f,g),h)dt=Cop_I(f,g,h). These identities hold piecewise in time and add across adjoining steps with their common endpoints. For every fixed tau>0, Ftau:L2_zero->H^1 and Psi_tau:L2_zero->L2_zero are continuous polynomial maps, preserve reality, and map smooth data to smooth data; all finite iterates are therefore well defined and continuous in L2.

inputs.statement: For every interval I=[a,b] in [0,infinity), |I|<=1, and mean-zero continuous piecewise smooth functions f1,f2,f3 with finite Xnorm(I), ||Cop_I(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C|I| product_j||fj||_X(I)+C||fi||_(L^infinity(I;H^(-pstar))) product_(j!=i)||fj||_(L^infinity(I;L2)) for each i=1,2,3. The same estimate holds for arbitrary continuous functions in Xnorm with L^infinity L2 regularity and a distributional time derivative in L^infinity H^(-pstar). For time-independent mean-zero fj in H^sigma, 0<=sigma<=1, ||Cop_I(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_sigma |I|^sigma product_j||fj||_(H^sigma), interpreted with the bounded extension. Constants are uniform in interval location and Fourier support.

For any smooth real mean-zero datum and integer L>=1, tau=T/L, the scheme iterates are smooth, real and mean-zero. With D023 on each step, v^(n+1)=f_n+F_n(t_(n+1))+C_n(t_(n+1))-Remainder_(t_n,tau)(f_n,f_n,f_n). Hence V(t_n)=v^n and V(t_(n+1))=v^(n+1), so V is continuous and piecewise smooth on [0,T]. Also Y_n'=Bop_t(f_n,F_n)+(1/2)Bop_t(F_n,F_n)-W_n/tau, Y_n(t_n)=0, and Rres is continuous, piecewise smooth with Rres'= -Bop_t(Y_n,z_n)-(1/2)Bop_t(Y_n,Y_n)-W_n/tau; consequently V'=(1/2)Bop_t(V,V)+Rres' on each step and distributionally globally. All V,Y_n,z_n,Rres and W_n are mean-zero.

Fix any step n, 0<tau<=1, a mean-zero numerical state f_n in L2 and mean-zero w in H^gamma with ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0. Define delta_n=||f_n-w||_2<=1 and q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n; use the step formulas D023 with this f_n, initially smooth. Then q_n<=2, ||f_n||_2<=M0+1, sup||F_n||_(H^1)<=C_(M0,gamma), sup||F_n-Stage_n(t;w)||_(H^1)<=C_(M0,gamma)*delta_n, sup||F_n||_(H^agamma)+sup||F_n||_2<=C_(M0,gamma)*q_n, and ||z_n||_X(I_n)<=C_(M0,gamma). Moreover sup||Bop_t(F_n,F_n)||_2<=C_(M0,gamma)*q_n, sup||Q_n||_2+||W_n||_2<=C_(M0,gamma)*tau*q_n, and sup||Dinv Bop_t(f_n,F_n)||_2<=C_(M0,gamma)*q_n. Suprema are over the step; constants are uniform in the step and support.

Under the step hypotheses explicitly stated below, with smooth states initially and the interpolation D023, sup_(I_n)||Dinv Y_n'||_2<=C_(M0,gamma) q_n, sup_(I_n)||Dinv Y_n||_2<=C_(M0,gamma) tau q_n, sup_(I_n)||Y_n||_2<=C_(M0,gamma) q_n, ||Y_n||_X(I_n)<=C_(M0,gamma) q_n and sup_(I_n)||Y_n||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(M0,gamma) tau q_n. These estimates are uniform in step and Fourier support. Here explicitly the hypotheses are 0<tau<=1, n>=0, mean-zero f_n in L2 and w in H^gamma, ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0 and delta_n=||f_n-w||_2<=1, q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n.

output.statement: For smooth real mean-zero initial data, 0<tau=T/L<=1 and an exact twisted solution v with sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, use D023 and suppose delta_n=||v^n-v(t_n)||_2<=1 at a step. Then sup_(I_n)||rho_n||_2<=C_(M0,gamma) tau q_n and ||Rres'||_(L^infinity(I_n;H^(-pstar)))<=C_(M0,gamma) q_n. For any I=[a,b] subset [0,T] starting at a grid point and having h=b-a<=1, define E_I=sup_I||e||_2 for e=v-V. If E_I<=1, then sup_(t in I)||Rres(t)-Rres(a)||_2<=C_(M0,gamma)(h+tau)(tau^gamma+E_I), ||e||_X(I)<=C_(M0,gamma)(tau^gamma+E_I), and ||v||_X(I)+||V||_X(I)<=C_(M0,gamma). The interval may end inside a step.

locals.declaration: Fix the exact twist v on [0,T] with sup H^gamma norm <=M0.
Fix M0 as the bound on the exact twisted flow.
Fix 0<tau=T/L<=1 with a positive integer L.
Fix the arbitrary step index n with delta_n<=1.
Fix I=[a,b] starting at a grid point, with h=b-a<=1 and possibly partial final step.
Set E_I=sup_I||v-V||_2; the extra premise E_I<=1 is L1.

locals.type: real shorthand for the D023 component q_n
locals.declaration: Throughout this unit q_n denotes the defined scalar tau^gamma+delta_n; delta_n is the L2 distance to the chosen comparison state. The tuple components F_n,z_n,C_n,Q_n,W_n,V,Y_n,rho_n,Rres refer exactly to D023.

argument.text: Fix smooth data, an exact twisted flow with H^gamma bound M0, and a step with delta_n<=1. Put w=v(t_n), so N009–N010 apply. In the first integral of rho_n, integrate Bop_t(Y_n,z_n) by N005's normal form, keeping both endpoints. The asymmetric Jop estimate and sup||Dinv Y_n||_2<=C tau q_n bound the endpoint terms by C tau q_n. The term integral Jop_t(Y_n',z_n) is <=tau*C q_n by the Dinv Y_n' bound and ||z_n||_2<=C. Since z_n'=(1/2)Bop_t(f_n,f_n), the other term is (1/2)Cop(f_n,f_n,Y_n). Apply N006 with the negative norm on Y_n: its first term is <=C tau q_n because f_n is constant with bounded Xnorm and ||Y_n||_X<=C q_n; its second term is <=C tau q_n by the small H^(-pstar) norm of Y_n. Thus the first integral of rho_n is <=C tau q_n, uniformly at every partial-step endpoint.

produces.statement: For every partial endpoint of the step, ||integral Bop_t(Y_n,z_n)dt||_2<=C tau q_n.

argument.text: For integral Bop_t(Y_n,Y_n), the same normal form gives endpoint terms <=C tau q_n^2 and derivative terms <=tau*C q_n^2 using the asymmetric Jop estimate, Dinv Y_n and Dinv Y_n', and ||Y_n||_2<=C q_n. Since q_n<=2 this is <=C tau q_n. The affine W_n term is <=||W_n||_2<=C tau q_n by N009. Thus sup||rho_n||_2<=C tau q_n. By N008, Rres'=-Bop_t(Y_n,z_n)-(1/2)Bop_t(Y_n,Y_n)-W_n/tau; N005's Bop negative-norm bound, N009–N010 and q_n<=2 give ||Rres'||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C q_n.

produces.statement: On a step with delta_n<=1, sup||rho_n||_2<=C tau q_n and ||Rres'||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C q_n.

argument.text: Now fix any interval I=[a,b] starting at a grid point, h<=1, and temporarily assume L1: E_I=sup_I||e||_2<=1. There are at most h/tau+1 intersected steps, each beginning within I, with delta_n=||e(t_n)||_2<=E_I because N008 gives V(t_n)=v^n. Sum F002 over complete steps and the final partial step to obtain sup||Rres(t)-Rres(a)||_2<=C(h+tau)(tau^gamma+E_I). Differentiating the exact twist gives v'=(1/2)Bop_t(v,v); subtract N008 to obtain e'=Bop_t(e,v-e/2)-Rres'. N005 bounds its negative norm by C E_I+C(tau^gamma+E_I), proving ||e||_X<=C(tau^gamma+E_I). The exact L2 bound gives ||v||_X<=C; then V=v-e gives ||V||_X<=C, since tau^gamma<=1 and E_I<=1. Discharge L1, retain its antecedent, and quantify over all intervals and flows.
